A kilogram of feathers and a kilogram of steel have the same mass, so neither is heavier. They both weigh the same — one kilogram.

The classic trick in this question is that people intuitively think steel is heavier because it's denser. But weight depends on mass, not density. Since both are exactly one kilogram, they weigh the same.
